title: Sci-fi RPG Exodus gets even more Mass Effect-like with its female lead, who they are calling Femjun
summary: Yup, it's official.
body: We've said previously that, for better or worse, the third-person sci-fi RPG Exodus looks a lot like Mass Effect. It's a characterization that developer Archetype Entertainment isn't shying away from—in fact, it seems to be actively embracing it with the reveal of the game's female protagonist, who they refer to as Femjun. I kid you not, this is not a name I've cooked up or run across on social media. It's right there on the Exodus website : "Meet Femjun! You’ve been waiting to see FemJun, and today we’re happy to say she’s finally here." Femjun is a very direct reference to Femshep, the female version of Commander Shepard in BioWare's Mass Effect trilogy. While the male version was effectively the default playable character through the first two games, BioWare took steps to put them on equal footing for Mass Effect 3. That effort included a vote to let fans decide the character's official face , which was subsequently used on alternate or inside covers of Mass Effect 3 packaging. Voiced by Jennifer Hale, Femshep became so popular that when BioWare dropped the Mass Effect Legendary Edition trailer, it was she who appeared most prominently . So, back to Exodus: Fenjum will be portr…

summary: And cubemaps. Which, thank god.
body: Here's a terrifying reminder that the cold hand of Death is on my shoulder: I'm pretty sure I first played Black Mesa back in 2012, at the tender age of 19. In the intervening 14 years, the fan-made Half-Life 1 remake has walked quite the road, including getting Valve's official blessing to sell itself—for money!—on Steam in 2015. And they're still going, the mad lads. Just yesterday, Black Mesa got a hefty major update "featuring visual upgrades, engine optimizations, and a complete interface overhaul". It's called the Anomalous Improvements Update and it's a real humdinger. The biggest improvement—if you are me, a man who tries to play basically everything on his Steam Deck these days—is the Steam Deck verification and much-improved controller support. The game will now recognise and let you use a gamepad right from the jump, rather than forcing you to faff around in settings, and generally seems like a rather seamless delight on Deck in the little bit of time I've mucked about with it. title: AMD introduces Capacity Aware Scheduling to the Linux kernel, which sure is the thing I'd do if I were introducing Zen 6 LP cores next year
summary: Any way that more efficiently uses cores has the thumbs up from me.
body: AMD's Vishal Badole recently posted two Linux kernel patches (via TechPowerUp ), and these both pair up to introduce Capacity Aware Scheduling (CAS) for AMD heterogeneous processors. If that sounds like gibberish to you, effectively, this lays the groundwork to more efficiently handle AMD chips that have different core types. Up until now, AMD's performance scaling driver for Linux (amd-pstate) treated all cores as equal, assigning tasks regardless of core strength. AMD's current heterogeneous design pairs full-fat Zen 5 and lower-caste Zen 5C cores together in Zen 5 chips nowadays, but there is far less actual difference between these two core types than in the P-cores and E-cores of modern Intel architectures. But Zen 6's full lineup is currently suggested to be quite different. Also shared in a Linux patch earlier this year , Zen 6 is set to introduce a new Low Power core type (which is set to run at a very low power, as you might guess from the name), and that is a core type that would really benefit from Capacity Aware Scheduling. What AMD has called Performance and Efficiency cores up until now is not the same as what Intel has called Performance and Efficiency cores. AMD's …

title: 'They would never stop working on this game': GTA 6's development could've gone on for longer just because 'it's really hard to close it down'
summary: There's always room for a bit more polish.
body: Working to a deadline is hard enough, but working towards one that can be moved if you really need it is worse. Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in the works for around a decade, including a couple of delays so devs could polish up some rough edges, and after all this time it must be really hard to step back and say enough is enough. "They would never stop working on this game if they had the choice," Jennifer Kolbe, head of publishing, says in an interview with The Guardian . (Image credit: Rockstar) We now know that part of the reason why GTA 6 was delayed was because of the sheer amount of NPCs that needed kitting out with dialogue and audio. Talking to Bloomberg co-head of Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, explained how the delay wasn't strictly necessary but not delaying would have meant GTA 6 "won't be the game we want to make." Nelson expands on this with The Guardian: "It’s really hard to close it down. If you step away and get a little bit of space from it, you can look at it objectively and go: 'I'm proud of what we’ve done'. body: World of Warcraft: Forever's having some teething issues with its new spellcaster itemisation. The idea, to sum it up quick, is that a lot of the power that was in spells innately has been pushed onto items, instead, with the intention to make it feel really good when you get a cool new staff as a mage, for instance. This has had unintended consequences, as discovered by Rextroy (the same madlad who solos raid bosses ), as shared on YouTube . The problem is this: Gear in Forever can give a lot of raw power to your healing and damage spells, as part of the aforementioned changes. But that raw power also applies to lower-level healing spells, too. In Forever (and in Classic), casting lower-level spells is a core part of managing your mana as a healer. In this instance, however, "the healing coefficient on healing power remains the same, which is around 43% [on a low level Flash of Light], so if I stack all healing green items, I get my healing power up towards 242," Rextroy explains. This suit alleges "Intel misled investors about demand for its products and the Company's future growth potential." The class action can involve anyone who bought stock between July 23, 2026, and October 29, 2026, known as the "class period". With the memory crisis in full effect, PC sales are down worldwide ( estimated to be 20% down in October ), but the lawsuit argues that the PC sales slowdown was "having a materially greater negative impact to Intel’s third quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Group results than defendants had disclosed to investors." title: Influential Warhammer miniature designer Aly Morrison has died
summary: Morrison retired just six months ago.
body: Miniature designer and artist Aly Morrison has died, as confirmed by Trish Carden Miniatures and Design on Facebook . Carden, Morrison's ex-wife and former partner in Marauder Miniatures, posted that, "Mharaid and I are heartbroken to announce the passing of Aly Morrison, a very much loved father, veteran wargames miniatures designer and friend to many around the tabletop and the world. Aly passed unexpectedly but peacefully this Wednesday, and will be sorely missed." Aly Morrison began sculpting for Citadel in 1983 as a freelancer before joining the studio full-time in 1986. He and Trish were then made stewards of Games Workshop's imprint Marauder Miniatures in 1988, where they had free reign to create quirky and characterful figures like the mohawked dwarf trollslayers and the giant with a whaler's beard and a booze barrel strapped to his waist that became archetypal parts of Warhammer. Morrison also crafted the first miniatures for Blood Bowl players and drew the tokens to represent them in the board game's first edition. title: Are you more of an ambient music enjoyer or theatrical atmosphere appreciator?
summary: Quiet and unassuming, or loud and proud?
body: When World of Warcraft: Forever's beta first launched, I lamented its long stretches of silence and penchant for ambience over theatrics. I still sort of stand by that, but after spending more time in Azeroth (and discovering the loop music setting) I've a new-found appreciation for both WoW's soundtrack and ambient music as a whole. It's also got me thinking about what makes a soundtrack ambient versus something more melodic. I'm chronically Final Fantasy 14-brained, where just about everything has a grand thematic soundtrack to it—the jauntiness of the Gold Saucer, the soothing Middle-earthness of Gridania's outer Shroud zones, the grand organs of Ishgard's bitterly cold landscape. You can't escape composer Masayoshi Soken's penchant for leifmotifs. He will turn anything into an orchestral spectacle. I'm a big JRPG fan in general, a genre I think is the absolute master of thematic soundtracks. But I also think fondly of games I've played over the years that are a little more pared down, their soundtracks there for a little atmosphere rather than actively driving the narrative. PC Gamer said as much back in March 2020. In a recent interview with PC Gamer associate editor Ted Litchfield, Jackbox Games CEO Mike Bilder said that the pandemic proved transformative for the developer. "The industry at large obviously saw a lot of success at that time, but we did as well, and we went from a gamer name to a household name," he said, noting it was an "unfortunate period of time for the world, but for the gaming industry, a good one, and for Jackbox, a good one as well." body: Disk Cleanup (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Stuart Ashen—better known by his YouTube persona Ashens—grew up on a diet of 8-bit games on consoles like the Atari 2600 and the Spectrum. The earliest PC game he recalls playing was Syndicate Wars on his first home-built rig—a Pentium 200 MMX machine housed in a server tower case: "I loved Syndicate . Hated Syndicate Wars. Never got on with it at all," he says. "Ended up giving it to a friend who loved it … I think I went on to Duke Nukem 3D or something." summary: I won't miss.
body: Slay the Spire 2 has a new character—notably, a new character in testing —and as the patch notes themselves point out , that testing will very much be needed: "We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch." I decided to hop into the beta branch myself and take her for a whirl, and—yeah, those changes'll have to come. The Fool's central mechanic is her bow and arrow—she can fire an arrow/shoot card to deal damage equal to the card's base damage plus her aim. So if a shoot card deals 15 damage and she has six aim stocked, she'll deal 21. This is a little busted, because by default, the Fool has 6 aim already put in her bank. Her non-strike starter card, Foolish Shot, already deals a hefty 15 damage for just one energy. With aim, the first time she uses it, it deals a whopping 21 damage, which is a heck of a damage output for the Fool's first round of combat. The saving grace here is that when a card that fires an arrow is used, that arrow becomes lodged in a target, who gains the Impale status. You can't play any more arrow-based cards until you either Dislodge (another game term, hence the proper nounage) an arrow with…

title: Former survival MMO Dune: Awakening can now be played 'without requiring an Internet connection at any point' as its much requested offline mode arrives
summary: Everything including 'creating and deleting single-player characters' can be done without touching the web.
body: At long last, the transfer of power is complete. Dune: Awakening , Funcom's ambitious survival MMO based on the classic sci-fi novel, has completed is pivot away from massive multiplayer, and can now be played fully offline. The offline function arrived in an otherwise unremarkable patch that mainly fixes specific bugs and technical issues. "It's now possible to play the game in single-player mode without requiring an internet connection at any point, including creating and deleting single-player characters.," Funcom revealed in a Steam post. Dune: Awakening has been gradually drifting away from being a purely multiplayer experience for some time. In April, Funcom made its PvP element, like the Deep Desert and shipwreck exploration, fully optional . A fully fledged single-player mode arrived in September, including a dramatic rework of several major endgame systems—like its dynamic political "Landsraad" system' to make them work in solo play. At that point, single-player still required an Internet connection. Now though, that's no longer the case. To be clear, Dune: Awakening can still be played with all its multiplayer and PvP trappings, now including a "Go Online" button for exa…

title: The most annoying questgivers in PC games
summary: The XP isn't worth it.
body: Moira Brown gets a bad rap. Fallout 3's most chipper NPC, the Minnesotan menace is an inventor who sends you out on fact-finding missions to investigate the many dangers of the Wasteland. That means she puts you in harm's way quite a lot, which many players hate her for. Others just hate her voice. I think her positive outlook makes a refreshing change of pace from, you know, everything else going on in Fallout 3. Plus she gives you an armored Vault suit just for starting her questline, and the Wasteland Survival Guide she writes with your help goes on to be a useful item in both New Vegas and Fallout 4. What I'm saying is, there are plenty of videogame questgivers much more annoying than Moira Brown. All of the ones below, for starters. And if you disagree, you're a big meanie. Zero Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Rockstar loves to make us sit through cutscenes where our protagonist agrees to help out some of the most annoying people alive. Zero isn't alone—in GTA: San Andreas, he's got wannabe MC/janitor OG Loc for competition—but he is the winner for absolute worst. title: GTA 6 soundtrack leak confirmed accurate with new songs from Lana Del Rey, Playboi Carti, and Keith Richards
summary: What, no Sideways Hank O'Mally?
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 is more leak than ship at this point, with the anonymous individual known as Cyberleek in particular responsible for feeding the hype machine in ways that Rockstar weren't big fans of. The latest leak came from elsewhere, however, via a video of someone handling advance copies of the vinyl soundtrack . The album's track listing is visible, and has been confirmed as accurate by Rolling Stone's sources as well as Billboard's . This is the soundtrack rather than the score, which will be by Justice—the French electronic duo responsible for the excellent 2007 electro house album Cross—though they do feature here a couple of times as well. Their songs Flower in a Hurricane (with Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard) and Starting from Zero (with Michael McDonald of the Doobie Brothers and Steely Dan) are both on side A. title: Planeswalker, Netflix's Magic: The Gathering animated series, will have a different art style for each plane
summary: "Each one of these cards is this window into this incredible world. It's not just world building—it's worlds building."
body: Netflix's Magic: The Gathering series was initially announced in 2019 with the MCU's Russo Brothers at the helm, though they left a couple of years later thanks to the all-purpose "creative differences". That was all we heard until 2024 until Brandon Routh, who had been cast as planeswalker Gideon Jura, casually mentioned in an unrelated interview that the project had been binned. Netflix announced soon after that actually the animated series was a go, now with Terry Matalas of Star Trek: Picard and the 12 Monkeys TV series as its head showrunner, with a teaser image showing pyromancer Chandra and leonin Ajani Goldmane silhouetted against a red sky. Now, a mere seven years after the first reveal, there's a "sneak peek" trailer with a bunch of excited Wizards of the Coast staff, art labeled "early development", and a few seconds of Ajani and Chandra doing their stuff. The most intriguing part is when, over a montage of 3D props including a car that looks like an art deco Batmobile from New Capenna, executive producer and supervising director Patrick Osborne says, "All the planes exist in their own pocket universe. That comes with culture, design language, architecture, and we're ev…
